nv_cuzcotopia.blurb: Cuzcotopia is a limestone sport wall high on the north side of Mount Potosi, part of the Comedy Crags zone outside Las Vegas. The rock is dark, banded with chert and sharp on the fingers, and a number of the lines run past 100 feet. Bolting is generous and most of the grades fall between 5.8 and 5.10, so it suits newer leaders as well as people on a mellow day. The wall faces north and stays shady, which can feel chilly in cooler months but is a relief when lower crags are baking. Getting there takes effort: a steady climb above the roadside walls, then a long traverse along the slope.
nv_cuzcotopia.approach: A trail starts just right of the left-hand roadside crag and gains roughly 400 feet by switchbacks and ledges. From the top, keep following it about a quarter mile along the hillside, passing smaller walls, until you are beneath the wall.

nv_subway_the.blurb: The Subway is the most developed bouldering zone on Mount Charleston, a pocket of steep limestone off the Route 158 road at roughly 8,000 feet. A big roof low enough to boulder beneath anchors the Main Cave, and more problems are scattered downstream in a section called the Sewers. The climbing is powerful and tends toward steep traverses and roofs, with problems spanning the easy-to-very-hard range but concentrated around V3 to V7. The area is shaded throughout the day, and the altitude keeps it cool, so it is a good summer escape from the valley heat. Bring several pads, since landings can be uneven.

nv_central_slab_area.blurb: The Central Slab is a gray, low-angle section of the Imagination Wall high in Kyle Canyon on Mount Charleston, at about 8,000 feet. The climbing is technical slab on small edges and runnels, nearly all of it bolted, with a few longer multi-pitch lines mixed in. The grade range runs from the upper 5.7s into the low 5.13s, but the core of the area is 5.10 to 5.12, with 5.11 the most common. It is a spot for balance and footwork rather than pulling hard, and the high elevation makes it a summer-season destination. The base is reached by following the foot of the cliff leftward over a couple of steep rises.

nv_robbery_wall_the.blurb: The Robbery Wall is the busiest face at Robber's Roost, a limestone sport crag off Route 158 on Mount Charleston. It is a tall, continuous wall tucked in the back corner above a large cave, and it is known for sustained, pumpy climbing and for the many extensions and link-ups that stack harder grades on top of the original lines. Almost everything here is 5.12 to 5.14, with a few entry points in the 5.10s and low 5.11s, so it mostly attracts strong sport climbers. The most popular lines can have queues on busy days, and the surrounding cliffs keep parts of the wall shaded.

nv_the_wake_up_wall_climbs.blurb: The Wake-Up Wall is a short, dense sandstone cliff near the Sandstone Quarry at Red Rocks, popular both as a warm-up and as a destination in its own right. The routes are punchy and often bouldery, mostly bolted, with a handful of trad lines and a boulder problem. Grades start around 5.8 but the bulk are 5.10 to 5.12. The wall stays in shade for much of the day in winter, though wind can find it, and a flat slab at the base makes a comfortable place to gear up. As everywhere at Red Rocks, the sandstone is fragile when damp.
nv_the_wake_up_wall_climbs.approach: From the Sandstone Quarry lot, take the Turtlehead Peak trail up the steep section, then veer left across slabs to the cliff base.

nv_great_red_book_area_the.blurb: The Great Red Book Area is a broad sandstone face in the Calico Hills at Red Rocks, reached from the second pullout on the scenic loop. It holds a mix of trad and sport routes, mostly long single pitches plus a few two-pitch lines, and the grades cluster around 5.8 with a good number of 5.9 to 5.10 as well. Because most routes are moderate, it makes a good objective for newer trad leaders. The sandstone is fragile when wet. Pullout parking is tight in busy season, so early starts or weekday visits help.
nv_great_red_book_area_the.approach: From the second pullout lot, pass through the Black Corridor and turn sharply up the ramp beneath the Hunter S. Thompson Dome. Continue past the Dome and Poser Crag, then climb the talus slope to the left to reach the base.

nv_panty_wall.blurb: Panty Wall is one of the most visited sport walls at Red Rocks, sitting a short walk from the first pullout on the scenic loop in the Calico Hills. The red sandstone holds a blend of bolted lines, some trad and a few top-ropes, with grades running from 5.5 up into the 5.12s. The 5.10 to 5.11 range is the most common, but there are enough easier routes to make it a solid choice for newer climbers. Because it sits so close to the road, it is busy, with tourists passing nearby and often several parties on the wall at once. Sandstone here is fragile when damp.
